title: Building a Cyberpunk RPG where you build real AI agents
author: Launchable-AI
selftext:
Hey all,

Wanted to share a game I'm working on.  The basic idea is that you build real AI agents, and work as part of a resistance network to take back control from the AI overlords.

I build AI agents professionally, and have been trying to figure out what parts of doing that and learning the skill are actually enjoyable.  I think anyone who has been vibe-coding for awhile will agree that continually prompting Claude or w/e isn't super fun.  But watching your stuff come to life is pretty rewarding.  Hence the game.

All of the assets are built with AI, driven mostly through Claude Code.  I use a variety of models through eg replicate to generate the images, audio, etc.  Continually looking for better methods and models, so if you have any advice, do share!

The NPCs are all driven by LLMs, so you can talk to characters in the game.  This is also a gameplay mechanic, with secrets, missions., etc, being linked to conversations.

The goal is to eventually have a large scale city simulation that is constantly adapting to what is happening in the game.

If you're interested in trying the game, or in learning how to build AI agents, try it out!

I just opened the game to public beta today (still going to be some rough edges).  I'd love any feedback!

Thanks!

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
Tying secrets and missions to conversations is the right call. It gives players a reason to actually talk to the NPCs instead of treating the chat box as a novelty.

On the city-simulation goal, one thing I learned the hard way: give each NPC a small amount of state that persists outside the chat (mood, money, who they're mad at) and feed it back into their prompt. Without it, characters reset to friendly every conversation and the city never feels like it's changing.

I'm the dev of a game in a similar space, Hatched, where an entire beach city runs on AI residents and you're the voice in one citizen's head. So the "city that adapts" part is close to my heart. How are you handling cost once lots of NPCs need to think at the same time? Do background characters only call the model when a player is nearby?

replies.author: Launchable-AI
replies.body:
Thanks for the comment.  And good luck with your game!

I am doing something like this already with dialogue.  The NPCs have an internal stage that gets persisted through the game.  So if you frustrate them or insult them in a chat for example, they’ll start behaving differently.  As things in the game change, the communicate and learn.

On cost optimization, this is a major open question.  I’ve been running tons of tests with different models, see which ones are cost effective and also work well.  I use several different LLMs for different systems in the game (eg writing code vs chatting with chars vs running the agents).  One of the major challenges is keeping this working well without going bankrupt lol

comments.body: one word of advice, some one put up AI heavy driver's ed game demo out and it started racking up $1000 a day in tokens. So if the game somehow went viral, they would have been bankrupted... or at least profitability would be massively crippled. This is also why Anthem failes. Operational costs can bite you!
